# Multi-Agency Response Scenario: Drone Swarm Attack on a Visiting U.S. Navy Vessel, Port of Albany, NY

**Status: Fictional training/tabletop-exercise narrative.** This is a hypothetical scenario for emergency-management planning, mutual-aid discussion, or exercise design — not a real event, and not a technical description of how to build, arm, or fly an attack drone swarm. The "attack" beats are kept deliberately vague; the value here is in the response, jurisdiction, and coordination problem it creates.

---

## Scenario setup

It's a Saturday afternoon in late summer. A U.S. Navy littoral combat ship — call it the fictional **USS Cohoes** — is on a scheduled public port visit at the **Port of Albany**, moored pier-side along the Hudson River south of downtown Albany. Public tours have been running since 10:00; roughly 600 civilians are aboard or queued on the pier, several hundred more are watching from Corning Preserve and the riverfront, and the water itself is crowded — a Hudson River sightseeing/dinner cruise boat, kayakers, a handful of personal watercraft, and a rowing club out for a Saturday session. The ship has normal in-port force protection posture: sentries at the brow, a small-boat security element patrolling the surrounding Coast Guard–designated safety zone, and magnetometer screening for tour visitors. The U.S. Navy vessel's standing FAA security restriction under 14 CFR § 99.7 / applicable security NOTAM is already active, including the UAS stand-off around the vessel. Because the visit was scheduled, Albany PD and New York State Police have pre-staged C-UAS detection/airspace-awareness systems and liaison personnel before public tours begin; detection and tracking capability is operational, while any mitigation authority remains separately controlled.

## Timeline

**T+0:00 (14:32)** — The pre-existing FAA naval-vessel security restriction and local/state C-UAS monitoring posture are already active. Topside watch, the ship security element, and pre-staged C-UAS sensors report multiple small UAS inbound low over the water, approaching from two directions — one group crossing from the Rensselaer side of the river, a second rising from a wooded rail-yard parcel near the port. A dozen-plus quadcopters in a loose, coordinated formation; several are visibly carrying attached payloads.

**T+0:01** — The ship sounds general quarters. The security boat broadcasts a warning and attempts to close, but the drones are faster to the ship than the response.

**T+0:02–0:04** — The lead group reaches the ship; explosions and impacts near the flight deck and the pier-side brow start a fire and cause structural and material damage. A second group breaks off toward the crowded water — one drone hits the sightseeing cruise boat near its stern, starting a fire and putting several passengers in the river; blast fragments and the resulting panic injure spectators on the pier and an adjacent riverside restaurant deck.

**T+0:05** — Not every drone is accounted for. Several scatter, and some go down in the river — which will matter later, because live or partially-functioned ordnance floating in a crowded waterway is its own hazard, and recovered wreckage is the only immediate physical evidence of who built this.

**T+0:06** — Albany County 911 is flooded with calls: an explosion on the Navy ship, a boat fire, people in the water, mass casualties on the pier.

**T+0:08** — First-due Albany Fire Department engine and Albany PD patrol units arrive and establish an initial command post at the foot of the pier. Albany FD requests a county-wide Mass Casualty Incident (MCI) activation.

**T+0:10** — The Coast Guard Captain of the Port (Sector New York, whose zone covers this stretch of the Hudson) is notified and issues an emergency safety/security zone, directing all remaining river traffic clear. Coast Guard small boats and Auxiliary vessels from the nearest stations get underway.

**T+0:12** — Albany County Emergency Communications activates the regional mutual-aid MCI plan, pulling ambulances from Rensselaer, Schenectady, and Saratoga counties. Albany Medical Center — the region's Level 1 trauma center — goes to disaster alert and opens surge capacity; St. Peter's Hospital and Samaritan Hospital (Troy) are notified as overflow receivers under the regional EMS council's patient-distribution plan.

**T+0:15** — NCIS agents (some already on-site for the port visit) move to secure the ship as a crime scene and begin securing witnesses among the crew. Albany PD/County notify the FBI's Albany Field Office, which will end up leading the federal criminal investigation once the scene stabilizes.

**T+0:18** — The FAA supplements the standing naval-vessel security restriction with a broader incident-specific emergency Temporary Flight Restriction (TFR) over the port and surrounding airspace. Local news helicopters are told to hold clear or coordinate through incident air operations.

**T+0:20** — The TFR is already being ignored. Hobbyist drones and independent livestreamers — some launching from Corning Preserve and the riverfront park just north of the security perimeter — start converging overhead to get footage. Incident command now has a second problem layered on the first: rogue civilian drones are cluttering the same airspace a medevac helicopter needs, and they make it harder for anyone to tell whether a given drone overhead is a gawker or a second wave. State Police aviation and additional C-UAS capacity are assigned to augment the detection systems already operating around the vessel — track, identify, correlate, and hand off violators for later FAA/law-enforcement follow-up while preserving the existing hostile-track picture.

**T+0:25** — NY State Police Troop G, the State Police Bomb Disposal Unit, and its Counter Terrorism Unit are dispatched. The State Emergency Operations Center goes to alert; the Governor's office and NYS DHSES are notified.

**T+0:30** — Unified Command stands up at a staging area on port property, with the ship's Commanding Officer (or designated liaison) and NCIS at the table alongside Albany Fire, Albany PD, Albany County Sheriff, the Coast Guard Captain of the Port's representative, the FBI, and Albany County Emergency Management. Rescue/EMS, hostile-threat/security, maritime, airspace, military force-protection, and investigative authorities remain concurrent rather than collapsing under a single functional agency.

**T+0:35–1:00** — Search and rescue continues for people who went into the river. Albany FD and State Police dive/underwater recovery teams are requested. DEC Police responds for a fuel sheen coming off the damaged vessels. Because nobody yet knows what the drone payloads actually were, the New York National Guard's WMD Civil Support Team is requested to do a technical CBRNE assessment before anyone treats the wreckage or the injured as anything other than a hazard.

**T+1:00–2:00** — Patients are distributed across the region under the EMS council's coordination. A press staging area goes up well back from the operational zone, and a Joint Information Center — Navy Public Affairs, FBI, Albany PD, Coast Guard — starts trying to get ahead of a story that a dozen people are already livestreaming badly from their own drones. At least one civilian operator is intercepted flying inside the TFR; several more are referred to the FAA after the fact from detection-system logs.

**T+2:00 onward** — The scene shifts from rescue to recovery and investigation. FBI (with NCIS on anything involving the ship or Navy personnel, and ATF if explosive residue is confirmed) starts drone-wreckage recovery and forensic exploitation — manufacturer, serials, telemetry, launch point. The Coast Guard holds the security zone and the port stays closed. State Police manage the gridlock on I-787 and the Dunn Memorial Bridge from both the evacuation and the crowds trying to drive down and see it. Albany County Emergency Management and the Red Cross open a family reunification center off-site.

---

## Who shows up, and why

**Federal — military**
- **U.S. Navy** — the ship's own force protection element, damage control and firefighting parties, the Commanding Officer as the on-scene federal authority for anything aboard the vessel.
- **Naval Criminal Investigative Service (NCIS)** — lead investigative authority for any crime against Navy personnel or property; secures the ship as a crime scene.
- **Naval Operational Support Center (the nearest reserve/support command, e.g., Schenectady)** — logistical and personnel support.
- **New York National Guard WMD Civil Support Team** — technical CBRNE assessment of unknown drone payload residue.

**Federal — civilian**
- **FBI (Albany Field Office / Joint Terrorism Task Force)** — presumptive lead for the federal criminal/terrorism investigation; Evidence Response Team; Hostage Rescue/SWAT if any ongoing threat is suspected.
- **U.S. Coast Guard (Sector New York, Captain of the Port)** — authority over the waterway itself; establishes the security zone, directs marine traffic, brings small boats and possibly a Maritime Security Response Team.
- **ATF** — explosives identification and post-blast forensics if any payload detonated.
- **DHS/CISA** — critical-infrastructure and port-security coordination; Homeland Security Investigations if there's a foreign or import angle to the drones themselves.
- **FAA** — maintains the standing naval-vessel airspace restriction, may issue or expand incident-specific restrictions, investigates unauthorized drone operations, and works Remote ID data with law enforcement to identify violators.
- **FEMA Region 2** — consequence-management and resource support if the response scales past state/local capacity.

**State**
- **New York State Police** — Troop G patrol, Aviation Unit, Bomb Disposal Unit, Counter Terrorism Unit, boat patrol.
- **NYS Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Services (DHSES)** — state EOC activation, resource coordination.
- **New York State Intelligence Center** — fusion-center support to the FBI/JTTF investigation.
- **NYS Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC Police)** — fuel/oil spill and waterway environmental response.
- **NYS Office of Fire Prevention and Control** — technical fire/hazmat support to local fire departments.

**County**
- **Albany County Sheriff's Office** — marine unit, patrol, county-wide jurisdiction on the river.
- **Albany County Department of Emergency Management** — County EOC activation, mutual-aid coordination.
- **Albany County Department of Health** — mass-casualty public-health response.
- **Albany County 911/Emergency Communications** — the actual nerve center tying all of the above together on shared or interoperable channels.

**Local — City of Albany and neighbors**
- **Albany Police Department** — initial patrol response, Emergency Response Team (SWAT), detectives, likely holds a co-lead role in Unified Command.
- **Albany Fire Department** — first-due engine/ladder companies, marine/fireboat response, hazmat team; likely holds the initial Incident Commander role.
- **Regional EMS providers** (Albany-area services plus mutual aid from Colonie, Bethlehem, Rensselaer, Watervliet, Menands, and beyond) — mass-casualty triage and transport.
- **Albany Medical Center, St. Peter's Hospital, Samaritan Hospital (Troy)** — primary and overflow trauma receivers under the regional EMS council's patient-distribution plan.

**Port and maritime**
- **Port of Albany / Albany Port District Commission** — port operations, harbor master, and site security; coordinates with the pre-staged local/state C-UAS posture without being treated as the legal owner of C-UAS authority.
- **Hudson River pilots and local tug operators** — vessel-handling assistance, and in the first minutes, genuinely useful extra hulls for pulling people out of the water.

**Volunteer/NGO**
- **American Red Cross / Salvation Army** — mass care, family reunification, responder rehab.

## The media and private-drone problem

This is the part that's easy to underweight in planning and hard to control in real time. The moment a Navy ship visibly catches fire on a river in front of hundreds of phone cameras, three separate populations of aircraft show up on top of an already-contested airspace:

- **Broadcast and cable news** — helicopters and, increasingly, their own drone units, arriving within the first 20–30 minutes and wanting the establishing shot from exactly the altitude and angle a rescue helicopter needs.
- **Independent operators** — hobbyists, local drone-club members, and freelance photojournalists who launch from public land just outside (or inside) the perimeter because nothing is physically stopping them, including attempts from locations outside the vessel's standing protected-airspace footprint before any broader incident-specific restriction is issued or fully communicated.
- **The event's own contracted media drone**, if the Navy or the port hired one for tour-day publicity — which is actually a potential asset here rather than a problem, if incident command thinks to fold its operator and footage into the response instead of shooing it away with everyone else.

The operational cost isn't hypothetical: every extra drone over the scene is one more object a counter-UAS detection system has to classify, one more thing a medevac pilot has to visually clear before descending, and one more reason the FBI/NCIS evidence team can't be fully sure the airspace is "hostile-drone-clean" before they start working the wreckage. In practice this is why the pre-staged counter-UAS detection posture remains a dedicated function from the outset and is augmented as the incident grows; it is specifically tasked with sorting gawkers from threats — that's a distinct job from the fire, the rescue, and the investigation, and it needs its own owner or it doesn't get done.

## A note on command structure

No single agency in this scenario has clean authority over the whole thing, which is exactly why it becomes a Unified Command problem rather than a single-IC one. The ship and its crew are federal jurisdiction (Navy/NCIS); the waterway is Coast Guard Captain-of-the-Port jurisdiction; the pier, the crowd, and the civilian injuries are Albany city and county jurisdiction; the airspace is FAA and, once weaponized drones are involved, FBI/JTTF jurisdiction. Nobody waits for that to get sorted out before responding — Albany Fire and PD are on scene and running the rescue within minutes, under standard NIMS/ICS practice, with a Unified Command post standing up within the half hour to bring the federal players in as formal partners rather than parallel, uncoordinated responses.

---

*Compiled as a discussion/training scenario. Agency names and jurisdictions reflect real New York/Capital Region emergency-response structure as of 2026; the vessel, the attack, and the event itself are fictional.*
